stories.headline: Metal manufacturer among 34 new Trumbull businesses registered in September
stories.summary: Thirty-four businesses with Trumbull addresses registered with Connecticut in September, Patch reports, spanning about 30 self-described categories. Newcomers include a fabricated structural metal manufacturer, a full-service restaurant, an auto repair shop, a sports instruction business, and a plumbing/HVAC contractor. The list draws from active Connecticut Business Registry filings and has not been independently verified by type.

stories.headline: Trump rallies Alabama for Tuberville and Marques, says he’ll return for Alabama–Georgia
stories.summary: In Mobile on Friday, President Trump urged support for Sen. Tommy Tuberville’s governor race and Trump-backed Rhett Marques in Alabama’s redrawn 2nd District, framing the stop as respect for early loyalists rather than a pure battleground play. He announced a return next Saturday for Alabama–Georgia and again asked supporters to treat him as if he were on the ballot. AP notes the stop also aims to juice Florida panhandle turnout for Byron Donalds.

stories.headline: Obama-appointed judge blocks Trump from firing court-appointed U.S. attorney in Washington
stories.summary: Judge Stanley Bastian issued a preliminary injunction reinstating Roger Rogoff as U.S. attorney for the Western District of Washington and barring the DOJ from treating his removal as lawful. The White House called it activist interference with Article II removal power; DOJ said it will seek an immediate stay and appeal. Conservatives argue a 1979 OLC opinion and Myers already confirm presidents can fire U.S. attorneys, including judge-appointed ones.

stories.headline: State Department accuses Senate Democrats of ‘grandstanding’ on Venezuela NABEP oil stake
stories.summary: Four Senate Democrats demanded a briefing and documents on a deal giving the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital rights to a 35% stake in Venezuelan producer NABEP via penny warrants, plus State preferential oil purchase rights. State says lawmakers knew the Oct. 1 briefing and papers were coming, then the Senate left town and postponed it; State still delivered the agreement folders. Democrats question whether OSC has statutory authority to take foreign equity.

stories.headline: DHS: ICE arrests more ‘worst of the worst’ — child-rape and sexual-abuse convicts
stories.summary: DHS said ICE yesterday arrested criminal illegal aliens convicted of statutory aggravated rape of a child, rape of a child, sexual battery of a minor, unlawful contact with a minor, and sexual abuse, naming cases from Massachusetts, Pennsylvania, California, and New York. Secretary Markwayne Mullin cast the sweeps as Trump’s mandate to remove predators before they can threaten Americans again. DHS points the public to its WOW.DHS.Gov tracker for more local cases.

stories.headline: Abbott celebrates $7.5 billion DHS reimbursement for Texas Operation Lone Star border costs
stories.summary: Gov. Greg Abbott on Friday celebrated a $7.5 billion DHS check covering Texas spending under Operation Lone Star during the Biden years, drawn from Trump’s State Border Security Reinforcement Fund. Abbott said Texas got about 75% of that fund and still expects roughly $3 billion more from DOJ to reach a $10 billion total. He framed the repayment as justice for taxpayers who “held the line when Washington would not,” weeks before his midterm reelection fight.

stories.headline: AT&T and Apple push carrier settings 72.1 as they chase iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular fix
stories.summary: Apple released AT&T carrier settings 72.1 and began requiring iOS 27.0.1 at setup for iPhone 18 Pro Max units as thousands still lose calls, texts, and data on AT&T. MacRumors says the carrier update may disable 5G Standalone on affected Pro Maxes as a mitigation while a longer fix is built; AT&T says it is “working with Apple.” Hardware replacement for some units remains a separate path Apple already confirmed.

stories.headline: Tesla Supercharger network tops 85,000 stalls across 9,000 sites
stories.summary: Tesla Charging said Friday the Supercharger network has passed 85,000 stalls and 9,000 sites and is “still growing,” sharing a chart from the 2012 launch through Oct. 2, 2026. TeslaNorth notes the buildout now serves non-Tesla EVs as NACS adoption spreads, so new stalls are capacity for a wider EV mix—not only Tesla drivers. No next milestone date was given; construction continues.

stories.headline: Jets–Bears preview: Geno Smith’s historic start meets Chicago’s mystery QB
stories.summary: Official Jets preview for Sunday in Chicago highlights Geno Smith’s franchise-best 110 passer rating through Week 3 (75.5% completions, 4 TD, 0 INT) against a Bears defense that leans single-high. Chicago still has not named a starter with Caleb Williams out; Ben Johnson says “the direction’s already been made” among Keenum and Bagent. Minkah Fitzpatrick is expected back as New York’s No. 2 defense prepares for heavy motion.

stories.headline: Berkshires foliage nears peak as cool, dry weather arrives for parade weekend
stories.summary: After a summer-like Friday, AccuWeather and local forecasters say a prolonged cool, dry stretch will accelerate Berkshire color into peak, especially at Mount Greylock and other North County highs. Saturday–Sunday look favorable for outdoor events including Sunday’s 70th Northern Berkshire Fall Foliage Parade. The Eagle notes the recent nor’easter’s wind damage to the season looks minimal compared with Vermont and White Mountain peaks already firing.

stories.headline: Lafayette homeowner shoots boy he believed was trying to enter his house; no charges yet
stories.summary: Lafayette, Colorado police say a homeowner on Sibon Circle fired Thursday night after someone allegedly tried to enter his home; the person shot was a minor taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. No one has been arrested or charged, and police say they are still investigating with no ongoing community threat. The neighborhood sits south of West South Boulder Road near Centaurus High School.

stories.headline: Octopus steals snorkeler’s Insta360 X5 and films tentacle-framed underwater shots
stories.summary: An octopus grabbed a snorkeler’s Insta360 X5 and swam off, capturing humorous footage framed by eight tentacles that Insta360 later amplified. Digital Camera World notes 360 capture kept usable video even when the underside blocked part of the sphere—something a flat camera would have lost. The clip is another reminder why curious cephalopods and full-sphere cams keep colliding underwater.
